verb-quiz-1.title: Week 4 Quiz: Foundations: Learn How to Learn

questions.prompt: be → V2 (past) (give both forms, separated by /)
She ___ going to the Salvadoran festival this Saturday. (be)
questions.explanation: She is going to the Salvadoran festival this Saturday. (be)

questions.prompt: He ___ a Honda Civic before he crashed it. (have)
questions.explanation: He had a Honda Civic before he crashed it. (have)

questions.prompt: Which word means “to give your attention to one thing”?
questions.explanation: focus: to give your attention to one thing. Focus on one sentence at a time.

questions.prompt: You learned a rule. Now _____ it by using it in a new sentence.
questions.explanation: apply: to use what you learned. Apply the rule by writing a new sentence about yourself.

questions.prompt: In “The helpful teacher has a book,” which word describes the teacher?
questions.explanation: Helpful is an adjective. It describes the noun teacher.

questions.prompt: Fix one word: “She have a brother in Colombia.” Write the complete sentence.
answers: She has a brother in Colombia.

verb-quiz-2.title: Week 5 Quiz: Digital Habits + Community Routines

questions.explanation: What do you do after class? (do)

questions.prompt: Last Sunday, she ___ a study plan for the week. (make)
questions.explanation: Last Sunday, she made a study plan for the week. (make)

questions.prompt: Your homework is finished. Click "Send" to _____ it to your teacher.
questions.explanation: submit: to send your work or information officially. Submit your answers before the timer runs out.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to open or enter a file, website, or building”?
questions.explanation: access: to open or enter a file, website, or building. You can access your lessons from any device.

questions.prompt: Fill in the question word: ___ did she close the pop-up? Because it asked for her password.
questions.explanation: Why asks for a reason. Because introduces a reason.

questions.prompt: Which question correctly asks about the person who created an app?
questions.explanation: Who asks about a person. Here, who is the subject, so we do not add did.

verb-quiz-3.title: Week 6 Quiz: Getting Around: Directions + Digital Safety

questions.explanation: Yesterday, I went to the library. (go)
Please come to the front desk. (come)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to arrive too late to catch the next bus, train, or flight”?
questions.explanation: miss a connection: to arrive too late to catch the next bus, train, or flight. If the bus is late, I might miss a connection.

questions.prompt: _____ Central Square and walk one block. (Meaning: to leave a bus or train at a particular stop.)
questions.explanation: get off at: to leave a bus or train at a particular stop. Get off at Central Square and walk one block.

questions.prompt: A coworker asks Rosa about her coffee habit at work. Which answer is correct?
options: I drink always coffee at work.
I always drink coffee at work.
Always I drink coffee at work.
answers: I always drink coffee at work.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: I always drink.

questions.prompt: Rosa checks the bus app on some days, but not on most days. Which word fits?
questions.explanation: Sometimes means on some days, not most days. Usually means most of the time. Never means not at all.

verb-quiz-4.title: Week 8 Quiz: Phone English + Family Connection

questions.prompt: Can you ___ me your phone number? (tell)
questions.explanation: Can you tell me your phone number? (tell)
You should say your name clearly. (say)

questions.prompt: _____ the school if your child will be absent. (Meaning: to reach someone by phone, email, or message.)
questions.explanation: contact: to reach someone by phone, email, or message. Contact the school if your child will be absent.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to answer or react to a message or question”?
questions.explanation: respond: to answer or react to a message or question. Please respond to the email within 24 hours.

questions.prompt: "You don't have to come to the bank. You can call the number on your card." What does this mean?
options: Coming to the bank is forbidden.
Coming to the bank is required.
Coming to the bank is optional.
answers: Coming to the bank is optional.
questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means it is not required. It is different from 'must not,' which means it is forbidden.

questions.prompt: Claudette is setting up her new phone at the library. Which sentence is correct?
options: She can video-calls her daughter for free.
She can video-call her daughter for free.
She can to video-call her daughter for free.
answers: She can video-call her daughter for free.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs (can, should, must) are always followed by the base verb with no changes.

questions.prompt: Have you ever ___ food to a neighbor? (take)
questions.explanation: Have you ever taken food to a neighbor? (take)

questions.prompt: We have ___ extra bags for the volunteers. (bring)
questions.explanation: We have brought extra bags for the volunteers. (bring)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to help or encourage someone or a cause”?
questions.explanation: support: to help or encourage someone or a cause. Our community supports local families in need.

questions.prompt: Each person can _____ time or effort to the community project. (Meaning: to give time, money, or effort to help something.)
questions.explanation: contribute: to give time, money, or effort to help something. Everyone can contribute in a small way to make things better.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Have you ever ___ to a city council meeting?" (V3 of 'be')
questions.explanation: After 'have you ever', always use V3. The V3 of 'be' is 'been'.

questions.prompt: "Have you ever called 311?" Claudette says no. What is the best reply?
questions.explanation: Short answer for Have you ever uses haven't (not didn't or don't).

questions.prompt: She is good at ___ in public. (speak)
questions.explanation: She is good at speaking in public. (speak)

questions.prompt: After discussing different meeting times, we hope to _____ everyone accepts. (Meaning: to make a decision that everyone involved accepts.)
questions.explanation: reach an agreement: to make a decision that everyone involved accepts. We hope to reach an agreement about the meeting time.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to tell others about something you think may be a problem”?
questions.explanation: raise a concern: to tell others about something you think may be a problem. I would like to raise a concern about the bus schedule.

questions.prompt: Sarah asks Diego what he is good at. Put the words in order. Words: I / am / good / at / cooking / fast
answers: I am good at cooking fast
questions.explanation: Good at + -ing. The verb after 'at' must end in -ing.

options: Don't sign without read the letter.
Don't sign without reading the letter.
Don't sign without to read the letter.
answers: Don't sign without reading the letter.
questions.explanation: 'Without' is a preposition. The verb after it must be -ing: without reading.

verb-quiz-7.title: Week 7 Quiz: Our Voice, Our Vote

questions.prompt: If you ___ a letter to the council, they will read it. (write)
questions.explanation: If you write a letter to the council, they will read it. (write)

questions.prompt: If I ___ an email to the mayor, her office will answer me. (send)
questions.explanation: If I send an email to the mayor, her office will answer me. (send)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to add your name to the official list of voters”?
questions.explanation: register to vote: to add your name to the official list of voters. Where can eligible residents register to vote?

questions.prompt: Citizens _____ leaders to represent them in government. On election day, each voter marks a ballot for their favorite candidate.
questions.explanation: elect: to choose a person for a position by voting. Citizens elect leaders to represent them in government.

questions.prompt: Carlos tells Ana about the extra Saturday night shift and the electric bill. Which if-part is correct?
options: If I will take the extra shift...
If I take the extra shift...
If I took the extra shift...
answers: If I take the extra shift...
questions.explanation: In First Conditional, the if-part uses present simple. Never use 'will' in the if-part.

options: If your name is on the list, you get a ballot.
If Carlos will work Saturday, he will pay the bill.
If I don't see you by 5, I will call you.
answers: If Carlos will work Saturday, he will pay the bill.
questions.explanation: 'Will' cannot appear in the if-part of a conditional. It should be: 'If Carlos works Saturday...'

verb-quiz-8.title: Week 15 Quiz: Fall Review + Class Party

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to change a planned event to a different time”?
questions.explanation: I need to reschedule my appointment.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to tell others about something you think may be a problem”?
questions.explanation: I would like to raise a concern about the bus schedule.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to keep money, time, or something else for a particular purpose”?
questions.explanation: I set aside a little money each payday.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to offer to do something without being paid”?
questions.explanation: She volunteers at the food bank every Saturday.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to plan how much money to spend”?
questions.explanation: Budget your money so you can pay all your bills.

verb-quiz-9.title: Week 11 Quiz: How Long + For and Since

questions.prompt: The smaller package ___ less than the large one. (cost)
questions.explanation: The smaller package costs less than the large one. (cost)

questions.prompt: Last week, we ___ less on groceries. (spend)
questions.explanation: Last week, we spent less on groceries. (spend)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to record or pay attention to something as it changes”?
questions.explanation: keep track of: to record or pay attention to something as it changes. I use an app to keep track of my spending.

questions.prompt: What is the _____ with tax and delivery? (Meaning: the full amount to pay, including extra charges.)
questions.explanation: total cost: the full amount to pay, including extra charges. What is the total cost with tax and delivery?

questions.prompt: Luis von Ahn sold reCAPTCHA to Google in 2009. He does not own reCAPTCHA now. Which sentence is correct?
options: He sold reCAPTCHA to Google in 2009.
answers: He sold reCAPTCHA to Google in 2009.
questions.explanation: A finished action with a specific past time (2009) needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.prompt: Yesenia chose her phone company three years ago, in 2023. She wants to say how long she has had it, using 'for'. What does she say?
options: I have had this company for since three years.
I have had this company for three years.
I have had this company for 2023.
answers: I have had this company for three years.
questions.explanation: 'For' takes a length of time (three years), not a starting year (2023).

verb-quiz-10.title: Week 12 Quiz: More, Less, the Most: Comparatives + Superlatives

questions.explanation: Yesterday, I bought the cheaper phone. (buy)

questions.prompt: This shop ___ the most affordable furniture. (sell)
questions.explanation: This shop sells the most affordable furniture. (sell)

questions.prompt: The shirt is too small, so I want to _____ it for a larger one. (Meaning: to return one item and get a different one.)
questions.explanation: exchange: to return one item and get a different one. I want to exchange this shirt for a larger size.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “money returned to a customer after a purchase”?
questions.explanation: refund: money returned to a customer after a purchase. The store gave me a full refund for the broken item.

questions.prompt: Rosa compares three ways to get to work. Which sentence is correct?
options: The Blue Line is the most fastest.
The Blue Line is the fastest.
answers: The Blue Line is the fastest.
questions.explanation: Superlatives need 'the' before them. Never add 'most' to an -est form.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Plan B is ___ expensive than Plan C." (Long adjective comparative: don't add -er.)
questions.explanation: Long adjectives use 'more' for comparatives. Never add -er to a long adjective like 'expensive'.

verb-quiz-11.title: Week 13 Quiz: How Much / How Many: Countable + Uncountable

questions.prompt: She ___ rice with dinner every day. (eat)
questions.explanation: She eats rice with dinner every day. (eat)

questions.prompt: Yesterday, I ___ some water after lunch. (drink)
questions.explanation: Yesterday, I drank some water after lunch. (drink)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to buy a large amount of something at one time”?
questions.explanation: buy in bulk: to buy a large amount of something at one time. Is it cheaper to buy in bulk?

questions.prompt: Compare the _____ before choosing a package. (Meaning: the cost for one standard amount, such as one ounce or one pound.)
questions.explanation: unit price: the cost for one standard amount, such as one ounce or one pound. Compare the unit price before choosing a package.

questions.prompt: Claudette calls Fabienne from the grocery store. Put her question in order. Words: How / much / milk / do / we / need
answers: How much milk do we need
questions.explanation: Milk is uncountable, so use 'how much.'

options: There is too much oil in the pan.
I have a lot of eggs at home.
She bought a few rice for dinner.
answers: She bought a few rice for dinner.
questions.explanation: Rice is uncountable. You cannot say 'a few rice.' Use 'a little rice' instead.
Did you see the apartment yesterday? (see)

questions.prompt: Where did you ___ the rental listing? (find)
questions.explanation: Where did you find the rental listing? (find)

questions.prompt: Do I _____ this housing program? (Meaning: to meet the requirements for something.)
questions.explanation: qualify for: to meet the requirements for something. Do I qualify for this housing program?

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “a form used to ask to rent a home”?
questions.explanation: rental application: a form used to ask to rent a home. What documents do I need for the rental application?

questions.prompt: Rosa wants to ask the landlord about the nearest bus stop. Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: Information questions need inversion: question word + verb + subject. 'Where is the bus stop?' is correct.

questions.prompt: Rosa wants to ask about the price of rent. Which question word does she use?
questions.explanation: 'How much' asks about price or an uncountable amount. 'How many' is for countable things like bedrooms.

questions.prompt: We have to ___ an apartment this week. (choose)
questions.explanation: We have to choose an apartment this week. (choose)

questions.prompt: The landlord doesn’t ___ tenants smoke inside. (let)
questions.explanation: The landlord doesn’t let tenants smoke inside. (let)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to compare possible choices carefully before deciding”?
questions.explanation: weigh your options: to compare possible choices carefully before deciding. It helps to weigh your options before signing a lease.

questions.prompt: I can't _____ an apartment in that area. (Meaning: to have enough money to pay for something.)
questions.explanation: afford: to have enough money to pay for something. I can't afford an apartment in that area.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "You ___ renew your lease. It is your choice." (Three words: not required.)
questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means it is not required. 'Can't' would mean it is forbidden, which is different.

questions.prompt: The sanitary code says who must provide heat. Put the words in order. Words: The / owner / has / to / provide / heat
answers: The owner has to provide heat
questions.explanation: 'Has to' shows the owner is required to provide heat.

verb-quiz-14.title: Week 18 Quiz: Landlord Calls + Repair Requests

questions.prompt: I need to report that the window ___ yesterday. (break)
questions.explanation: I need to report that the window broke yesterday. (break)

questions.prompt: Could you ___ the door open, please? (hold)
questions.explanation: Could you hold the door open, please? (hold)

questions.prompt: The landlord will _____ the apartment next Monday. (Meaning: to look at something carefully to check its condition.)
questions.explanation: inspect: to look at something carefully to check its condition. The landlord will inspect the apartment next Monday.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “a message or form asking for a building or appliance to be checked or fixed”?
questions.explanation: maintenance request: a message or form asking for a building or appliance to be checked or fixed. I submitted a maintenance request for the broken lock.

questions.prompt: Rosa calls about an apartment on Lexington Street. Put the words in order. Words: I / would / like / to / meet / the / landlord
answers: I would like to meet the landlord
questions.explanation: 'Would like to' + base verb is the polite form. Use it for calls with landlords and offices.

options: I want finding an apartment near the bus.
I want to finding an apartment near the bus.
I want to find an apartment near the bus.
answers: I want to find an apartment near the bus.
questions.explanation: After 'want', use 'to' + base verb. 'Finding' (-ing form) is not correct here.

questions.prompt: I was cooking when I ___ a loud noise. (hear)
questions.explanation: I was cooking when I heard a loud noise. (hear)

questions.prompt: While I was locking the door, my neighbor ___ the building. (leave)
questions.explanation: While I was locking the door, my neighbor left the building. (leave)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to stop something from happening”?
questions.explanation: prevent: to stop something from happening. What steps can help prevent this problem from happening again?

questions.prompt: Will the landlord _____ me for the approved repair? (Meaning: to pay someone back for money they spent on an expense.)
questions.explanation: reimburse: to pay someone back for money they spent on an expense. Will the landlord reimburse me for the approved repair?

questions.prompt: Lucia was mopping the floor when the pipe burst. Which action was already in progress?
questions.explanation: Past continuous (was mopping) shows the background action in progress. Past simple (burst) is the event that interrupted it.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "While Lucia ___ the landlord, the kids woke up." (Action in progress: past continuous.)
questions.explanation: 'While' introduces the action that was in progress, so past continuous (was calling) is needed. 'Called' would use past simple.

questions.prompt: Before I applied, I had ___ a team leader. (become)
questions.explanation: Before I applied, I had become a team leader. (become)

questions.prompt: She had ___ two projects before her promotion. (lead)
questions.explanation: She had led two projects before her promotion. (lead)

questions.prompt: My _____ changes when my class schedule changes. (Meaning: the times when someone is free to work or meet.)
questions.explanation: availability: the times when someone is free to work or meet. My availability changes when my class schedule changes.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “a duty or task someone is expected to take care of”?
questions.explanation: responsibility: a duty or task someone is expected to take care of. Checking the supplies is my responsibility.

questions.prompt: When the manager arrived, I had already finished my tasks. What happened first?
options: Both happened at exactly the same time.
questions.explanation: Had finished marks the earlier past action.

questions.prompt: Gloria finished her tasks before the manager arrived. Put the words in order. Words: She / had / finished / before / the / manager / arrived
answers: She had finished before the manager arrived
questions.explanation: Past Perfect (had finished) = the earlier action. Past Simple (arrived) = the later action.

verb-quiz-17.title: Week 21 Quiz: Used to: Past Jobs and Routines

questions.explanation: You must wear safety shoes here. (wear)

questions.prompt: Employees have to ___ the exit clear. (keep)
questions.explanation: Employees have to keep the exit clear. (keep)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to work more than your usual scheduled hours”?
questions.explanation: work overtime: to work more than your usual scheduled hours. I used to work overtime during the busy season.

questions.prompt: A photo ID is _____ to enter the building. (Meaning: necessary; must be done.)
questions.explanation: required: necessary; must be done. A photo ID is required to enter the building.

questions.prompt: Linh used to walk to work, but now she takes two buses. What does "used to" describe in sentences like this?
options: Something that is still true today
A past habit or state that ended
answers: A past habit or state that ended
questions.explanation: Used to + base verb describes something from the past that changed.

questions.prompt: Linh starts work at 5 AM now. Back home, she started at 8. Which negative sentence is correct?
options: I didn't used to start work at 5.
I didn't use to start work at 5.
I don't use to start work at 5.
answers: I didn't use to start work at 5.
questions.explanation: Negative: didn't use to (no -d on use).

questions.prompt: If I ___ a free trip, I would visit my family. (win)
questions.explanation: If I won a free trip, I would visit my family. (win)

questions.prompt: If she ___ to Boston, I would meet her at the airport. (fly)
questions.explanation: If she flew to Boston, I would meet her at the airport. (fly)

questions.prompt: Can you _____ at the front desk while I answer this call? (Meaning: to help someone with something.)
questions.explanation: help out: to help someone with something. My coworker helped out when the front desk got busy.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to feel excited about something in the future”?
questions.explanation: look forward to: to feel excited about something in the future. We are looking forward to the long weekend.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "If I ___ you, I would talk to Jennifer." (Giving advice: use 'were' for all subjects.)
questions.explanation: In 'If I were you,' use 'were' for all subjects in the second conditional if-clause, not 'was' or 'am'.

questions.prompt: Marta is likely to get overtime next week. Which sentence fits?
options: If they offered me overtime, I would say yes.
If they offer me overtime, I will say yes.
If they offered me overtime, I will say yes.
answers: If they offer me overtime, I will say yes.
questions.explanation: A real, likely future situation uses the first conditional: 'if + present simple, will + base verb'.

verb-quiz-19.title: Week 23 Quiz: Enjoy Doing vs. Want to Do at Work

questions.prompt: Please ___ the boxes away after your shift. (put)
questions.explanation: Please put the boxes away after your shift. (put)

questions.prompt: Yesterday, I ___ along well with the new team. (get)
questions.explanation: Yesterday, I got along well with the new team. (get)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to arrive at work and record your start time”?
questions.explanation: clock in: to arrive at work and record your start time. I always clock in when my shift starts.

questions.prompt: Please _____ when your shift ends. (Meaning: to leave work and record your end time.)
questions.explanation: clock out: to leave work and record your end time. Please clock out when your shift ends.

questions.prompt: Marisol talks about her restaurant job and her goals. Put the words in order. (One verb needs a gerund, one needs an infinitive.) Words: She / enjoys / working / and / wants / to / learn
answers: She enjoys working and wants to learn
questions.explanation: Enjoy takes a gerund (working). Want takes an infinitive (to learn). Both are used correctly here.

questions.prompt: Elena says: 'I enjoy ___ to the guests.' Which form is correct?
questions.explanation: Enjoy always takes a gerund (verb + -ing). You cannot say 'enjoy to talk'.

questions.prompt: I have already ___ the safety rules. (understand)
questions.explanation: I have already understood the safety rules. (understand)
What does this job title mean? (mean)

questions.prompt: Include a _____ explaining why you are a good fit. (Meaning: a letter explaining why you want the job.)
questions.explanation: cover letter: a letter explaining why you want the job. Include a cover letter explaining why you are a good fit.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “a person who can speak about your work or character”?
questions.explanation: reference: a person who can speak about your work or character. My former boss agreed to be a reference for me.

questions.prompt: Rosa's phone buzzed 30 seconds ago. It's an email from HR. Which sentence fits?
options: HR sent an email last week.
HR has just sent an email.
HR hasn't sent an email yet.
answers: HR has just sent an email.
questions.explanation: Just means a very short time ago. The email is new news: HR has just sent an email.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "I haven't heard back from the hotel ___." (Not done, but expected.)
questions.explanation: Yet goes at the end of a negative or a question. It means up to now, but we expect it.

questions.prompt: Our team has been ___ steadily this year. (grow)
questions.explanation: Our team has been growing steadily this year. (grow)

questions.prompt: I have been ___ my computer skills. (build)
questions.explanation: I have been building my computer skills. (build)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “something treated as more important or urgent than other things”?
questions.explanation: priority: something treated as more important or urgent than other things. Finishing the application is my top priority today.

questions.prompt: It is smart to save money in an _____ for unexpected costs. (Meaning: money saved for unexpected problems.)
questions.explanation: emergency fund: money saved for unexpected problems. It is smart to save money in an emergency fund for unexpected costs.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has a grammar error?
options: She has been working at the hotel for two years.
How long have you been waiting for the bus?
He have been saving money since January.
answers: He have been saving money since January.
questions.explanation: With 'he,' use 'has been,' not 'have been.' The correct sentence is: He has been saving money since January.

questions.prompt: Rosa asks Amara about her work at the hospital. Put the words in order. Words: How / long / have / you / been / cleaning / patient / rooms
answers: How long have you been cleaning patient rooms
questions.explanation: PPC questions follow: How long + have/has + subject + been + verb-ing?

verb-quiz-22.title: Week 26 Quiz: Past Perfect Continuous + Work Experience

questions.prompt: I want to ___ you my work. (show)
questions.explanation: I want to show you my work. (show)

questions.prompt: Workers discussed their _____ to a safe workplace. (Meaning: something a person is entitled to do or have.)
questions.explanation: right: something a person is entitled to do or have. Workers discussed their right to a safe workplace.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to speak up for yourself or others”?
questions.explanation: advocate: to speak up for yourself or others. You need to advocate for yourself if you want a raise.

questions.prompt: Nadine ___ (work) nights for two years when the schedule changed. Use had been + -ing.
questions.explanation: had been working. Count duration up to the stated time.

questions.prompt: Minh ___ (clean) rooms for three hours when his break started. Use the past perfect continuous.
questions.explanation: had been cleaning. Count duration up to the stated time.

verb-quiz-23.title: Week 27 Quiz: Passive Voice + Pay Stubs

questions.prompt: The instructions were ___ to every employee. (give)
questions.explanation: The instructions were given to every employee. (give)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to choose what to do after considering the options”?
questions.explanation: make a decision: to choose what to do after considering the options. We need to make a decision about the schedule.

questions.prompt: Losing your job can be a serious _____ of violating safety rules. (Meaning: a result or effect of an action.)
questions.explanation: consequence: a result or effect of an action. Losing your job can be a serious consequence of violating safety rules.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Two shifts ___ moved without notice." (was or were?)
questions.explanation: 'Two shifts' is plural, so the passive form is 'were moved.'

options: My check was short last Friday.
questions.explanation: 'Three shifts' is plural, so the correct form is 'were moved,' not 'was moved.'

questions.prompt: If you ___ dizzy, you should sit down. (feel)
questions.explanation: If you feel dizzy, you should sit down. (feel)

questions.prompt: You should ___ more when you are tired. (sleep)
questions.explanation: You should sleep more when you are tired. (sleep)

questions.prompt: I called the clinic to ask where I could _____. (Meaning: to try to get help from a healthcare professional.)
questions.explanation: seek care: to try to get help from a healthcare professional. I called the clinic to ask where I could seek care.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “a later visit to check progress or discuss what happens next”?
questions.explanation: follow-up appointment: a later visit to check progress or discuss what happens next. When is my follow-up appointment?

options: You must not drive after this medicine.
You should rest for two days.
You should to call your supervisor.
answers: You should to call your supervisor.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is followed by the base verb without 'to': should call, not should to call.

questions.prompt: The doctor says: "You had better not go back to work until Thursday." Why does he use 'had better'?
options: He's being polite and it's just a suggestion.
He's giving a strong warning. If she goes back, something bad will happen.
He's talking about what she did in the past.
answers: He's giving a strong warning. If she goes back, something bad will happen.
questions.explanation: Had better signals a warning. There is a bad consequence if she ignores the advice.

questions.prompt: I stopped walking because I ___ yesterday. (fall)
questions.explanation: I stopped walking because I fell yesterday. (fall)

questions.prompt: My knee ___ when I bend it. (hurt)
questions.explanation: My knee hurts when I bend it. (hurt)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to get better after an illness, injury, or difficult experience”?
questions.explanation: recover from: to get better after an illness, injury, or difficult experience. It took me several weeks to recover from the surgery.

questions.prompt: The pain began to _____ yesterday. (Meaning: to become less strong or severe.)
questions.explanation: ease up: to become less strong or severe. The pain began to ease up yesterday.

questions.prompt: Marisol was working on the warehouse floor. At noon, she stopped ___ her pill. (She paused her work to take the pill.)
questions.explanation: 'Stop to take' means pause your current activity in order to do something else. Two different actions.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Jennifer asks: 'Did you take your pill this morning?' Marisol says: 'Yes, I remember ___ it at 7 AM.'" (She is recalling a past memory.)
questions.explanation: 'Remember taking' = recalling a past event. Something that already happened.

verb-quiz-26.title: Week 30 Quiz: The Doctor Said + Catch-Up

questions.prompt: The nurse said she ___ beside me during the test. (sit: simple past)
questions.explanation: The nurse said she sat beside me during the test. (sit: simple past)

questions.prompt: The doctor said I should ___ up slowly. (stand)
questions.explanation: The doctor said I should stand up slowly. (stand)

questions.prompt: It took me several weeks to _____ the surgery. (Meaning: to get better after an illness, injury, or difficult experience.)
questions.explanation: recover from: to get better after an illness, injury, or difficult experience. It took me several weeks to recover from the surgery.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to reduce how much you use, do, or consume”?
questions.explanation: cut back on: to reduce how much you use, do, or consume. I am trying to cut back on soda.

questions.prompt: Report this yesterday: The doctor said, “I am busy.” Complete: The doctor said that she ___ busy. Use past-tense backshift.
questions.explanation: With past-tense backshift, am becomes was.

questions.prompt: Marco reports what the pharmacist said about Amina's inhaler. Put the words in order. Words: The / pharmacist / told / me / to / keep / the / inhaler / inside
answers: The pharmacist told me to keep the inhaler inside
questions.explanation: Commands in reported speech use told + person + to + base verb.

questions.prompt: If I had not ___ my medicine, I would have felt better. (forget)
questions.explanation: If I had not forgotten my medicine, I would have felt better. (forget)

questions.prompt: If she had ___ the label, she would have noticed the warning. (read)
questions.explanation: If she had read the label, she would have noticed the warning. (read)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “a healthcare professional who prepares medicines and explains their use”?
questions.explanation: pharmacist: a healthcare professional who prepares medicines and explains their use. The pharmacist answered my questions about the label.

questions.prompt: Could there be an _____ between these medicines? (Meaning: a change in a medicine's effect when it is taken with another substance.)
questions.explanation: interaction: a change in a medicine's effect when it is taken with another substance. Could there be an interaction between these medicines?

questions.prompt: Yemi did not rest her knee when it started to hurt, and it got worse. Which sentence matches her situation?
options: If I rest my knee, it won't get worse.
If I had rested my knee, it wouldn't have gotten worse.
If I rested my knee, it wouldn't get worse.
answers: If I had rested my knee, it wouldn't have gotten worse.
questions.explanation: Third conditional uses if + had + V3 for a past action that did not happen.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a correct third conditional?
options: If Yemi rested more, she will have healed faster.
If Yemi had rested more, she would have healed faster.
If Yemi has rested more, she would heal faster.
answers: If Yemi had rested more, she would have healed faster.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: if + had + V3, would have + V3.

verb-quiz-28.title: Week 32 Quiz: Future Perfect + Wellness Goals

questions.explanation: I used to run every morning. (run)

questions.prompt: Now she ___ her bike to work. (ride)
questions.explanation: Now she rides her bike to work. (ride)

questions.prompt: I wrote down each _____ before my appointment. (Meaning: a change in how someone feels or functions that may indicate a health problem.)
questions.explanation: symptom: a change in how someone feels or functions that may indicate a health problem. I wrote down each symptom before my appointment.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “the agreed steps for managing a health condition”?
questions.explanation: treatment plan: the agreed steps for managing a health condition. At my next visit, I will ask about my treatment plan.

questions.prompt: By the end of May, Beatriz ___ (complete) her walking plan. Use the future perfect.
questions.explanation: will have completed. Look at the completed result by a future deadline.

questions.prompt: By Thursday, I ___ (do) my English homework. Use the future perfect.
questions.explanation: will have done. Look at the completed result by a future deadline.

verb-quiz-29.title: Week 33 Quiz: Be Used to + Still Adjusting

questions.prompt: I am used to ___ in city traffic. (drive)
questions.explanation: I am used to driving in city traffic. (drive)

questions.prompt: She is getting used to ___ up early. (wake)
questions.explanation: She is getting used to waking up early. (wake)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to relax after work, stress, or activity”?
questions.explanation: unwind: to relax after work, stress, or activity. I listen to music to unwind after work.

questions.prompt: Deep breathing is one of my _____ for stress. (Meaning: ways to handle stress or problems.)
questions.explanation: coping skills: ways to handle stress or problems. Deep breathing is one of my coping skills for stress.

questions.prompt: Mark describes Fabienne's routine. Put the words in order. Words: She / is / used / to / working / nights
answers: She is used to working nights
questions.explanation: Be used to + gerund (working) means it feels familiar or normal now.

questions.prompt: Fabienne eats dinner at 1 AM after her shift every night. Which sentence is correct?
options: I'm used to eat dinner very late.
I'm used to eating dinner very late.
I used to eating dinner very late.
answers: I'm used to eating dinner very late.
questions.explanation: Be used to needs a gerund: eating, not eat.

verb-quiz-30.title: Week 34 Quiz: All Four Conditionals + One Bad Week

questions.prompt: If I ___ my keys yesterday, I would have called you. (lose: use the past perfect)
questions.explanation: If I had lost my keys yesterday, I would have called you. (lose: use the past perfect)

questions.prompt: If I ___ my finger, I will clean it. (cut)
questions.explanation: If I cut my finger, I will clean it. (cut)

questions.prompt: The nurse asked whether I had been drinking enough _____. (Meaning: liquids, including drinks such as water, tea, or broth.)
questions.explanation: fluids: liquids, including drinks such as water, tea, or broth. The nurse asked whether I had been drinking enough fluids.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to gradually stop having an effect”?
questions.explanation: wear off: to gradually stop having an effect. I asked the pharmacist when the effect might wear off.

questions.prompt: Yemi says: 'If I earned more, I would move to a bigger apartment.' What do we know about Yemi?
options: She earns enough and is moving soon.
She moved to a bigger apartment last year.
She does not earn enough now. The move is imaginary.
She will earn more next month for sure.
answers: She does not earn enough now. The move is imaginary.
questions.explanation: Second conditional describes an imaginary situation now. The past-looking verb (earned) does not mean real past.

questions.prompt: Brian posts a rule in the break room. It is always true. Complete it: "If the warehouse door stays open, the loading dock ___ (get) cold."
questions.explanation: Zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple. Used for facts and rules.

verb-quiz-31.title: Week 35 Quiz: Future Perfect Continuous + Year-End Progress

questions.prompt: We plan to ___ our new routine tomorrow. (begin)
questions.explanation: We plan to begin our new routine tomorrow. (begin)
He is thinking about quitting smoking. (quit)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “to improve or move closer to a goal”?
questions.explanation: make progress: to improve or move closer to a goal. I make progress when I practice regularly.

questions.prompt: Support from classmates can help you _____. (Meaning: to successfully deal with something difficult.)
questions.explanation: overcome a challenge: to successfully deal with something difficult. Support from classmates can help you overcome a challenge.

questions.prompt: By next month, I ___ (learn) English for a year. Use the future perfect continuous.
questions.explanation: will have been learning. Count duration up to the stated time.

questions.prompt: By next month, we ___ (study) together for a year. Use the future perfect continuous.
questions.explanation: Keep the helper words together: will have been studying.

verb-quiz-32.title: Week 36 Bonus Quiz 1: All the Tenses: A Year in Review

questions.explanation: Someone stole my bike last year. (steal)

questions.prompt: This job offers many opportunities for personal _____. (Meaning: getting better over time.)
questions.explanation: growth: getting better over time. This job offers many opportunities for personal growth.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “feeling sure of yourself”?
questions.explanation: confident: feeling sure of yourself. She feels confident that she will pass the exam.

questions.prompt: Rosa already filled out the Level 4 form. Put the words in order. Words: She / is / going / to / take / evening / classes / in / September
answers: She is going to take evening classes in September
questions.explanation: Going to is for a plan that is already decided. Rosa filled out the form, so the plan is made.

questions.prompt: I ___ (work) for two hours when my break started. Use the past perfect continuous.
questions.explanation: The complete verb phrase is had been working.

verb-quiz-33.title: Week 36 Bonus Quiz 2: All the Tenses: A Year in Review

questions.prompt: She has ___ the early bus all week. (catch)
questions.explanation: She has caught the early bus all week. (catch)

questions.prompt: They ___ for better working conditions last year. (fight)
questions.explanation: They fought for better working conditions last year. (fight)

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “a promise to keep doing something”?
questions.explanation: commitment: a promise to keep doing something. Learning English takes real commitment and practice.

questions.prompt: I _____ all the help my teacher gave me this year. (Meaning: to be thankful for something.)
questions.explanation: appreciate: to be thankful for something. I appreciate all the help my teacher gave me this year.

questions.prompt: By Friday, I ___ (finish) my plan. Use the future perfect.
questions.explanation: The complete verb phrase is will have finished.

questions.prompt: By June, I ___ (study) here for about nine months. Use the future perfect continuous.
questions.explanation: The complete verb phrase is will have been studying.

verb-quiz-34.title: Week 36 Bonus Quiz 3: All the Tenses: A Year in Review

questions.explanation: The ball hit the window yesterday. (hit)
Could you lend me a pen? (lend)

questions.prompt: I want to _____ for my next English class. (Meaning: to decide on something you want to achieve.)
questions.explanation: set a goal: to decide on something you want to achieve. I want to set a goal for my next English class.

questions.prompt: Which word or phrase means “something you did well or completed”?
questions.explanation: achievement: something you did well or completed. Winning the award was a great achievement.

questions.prompt: Rosa is texting the babysitter at work right now. Which sentence fits?
options: She texts the babysitter at work.
She is texting the babysitter at work.
She has texted the babysitter at work.
answers: She is texting the babysitter at work.
questions.explanation: Present continuous for an action in progress right now.

questions.prompt: Find the error: "I have lived here since 2021."
questions.explanation: Present perfect with 'since' connects a past start to now.
